site_name: Centersquare EWR2 (fka Savvis/CenturyLink NJ2X, Cyxtera EWR2), 1919 Park Avenue, Weehawken, NJ 07086

year_site_match: The Savvis release names the NJ2X facility in Weehawken, N.J., adjacent to NJ2. verification: Savvis release dated June 23, 2010 announces completion of NJ2X and refers to 'the opening of NJ2X'; DCK (July 29, 2009) said Savvis had leased space adjacent to NJ2 with the first phase due by Q2 2010, consistent. Held at medium, not high, because of an unresolved conflict: the ENERGY STAR registry lists 'EWR2-C and D (Weehawken, NJ)', Centersquare, 209,237 sq ft, year constructed 2005, with no street address. I could not determine whether C and D are at 1919 Park Avenue or 300 Boulevard East, or whether 2005 is a shell year. This is inference, not verified: the 2009 DCK wording (leased space, build-out spending) suggests a fit-out of an existing building, so a 2005 shell year would not contradict a 2010 data center start. The release does not say customers were installed in NJ2X on that date.

year_evidence_quote: Amazon's three massive central Ohio data centers are up and running
year_site_match: The City of Dublin economic development page names the centers 'in Hilliard, Dublin and New Albany' as part of Amazon Web Services. The City of Dublin West Innovation District rezoning page (2025 update) says staff met with Amazon Web Services about sound from 'their existing facility on Houchard Road'. Area Development (June 2, 2015) and a Sept 28, 2015 construction write-up describe a single Dublin site of about 68-70 acres offered by the city. No page opened names the SR 161 intersection or the building ID CMH051.
verification: The City page (a repost of an Oct 18, 2016 Columbus Dispatch story; the Dispatch original could not be fetched) says the Dublin AWS center was up and running in October 2016. 2016 is the year for the first building on Amazon's Dublin campus. Held at medium for two reasons. First, the tie to Houchard Rd comes from a separate 2025 City page that refers to one existing AWS facility on Houchard Road; the same page also says 'existing facilities in Dublin' (plural), so I cannot rule out more than one AWS parcel there. Second, no page opened identifies CMH051; if the dataset treats CMH051 as a later building rather than the campus, 2016 is the campus start year, not that building's. A DCD page that might name the intersection returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

lead.year_evidence_quote: Amazon's central Ohio data centers now open
lead.notes: The City of Dublin econ-dev page dated Oct 18, 2016 says the Hilliard, Dublin and New Albany AWS centers are now open and up and running.
